description: The image displays two side-by-side bar charts illustrating Fleiss Kappa scores under different ambiguity conditions, both charts using a linear scale for the vertical axis labeled "Fleiss Kappa" ranging from 0.0 to 0.8, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The left chart, titled implicitly by its x-axis label "Ambiguity Std," shows three bars corresponding to x-axis values of 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94, with bar heights representing Fleiss Kappa values of 0.88, 0.46, 0.03, and 0.24, respectively; the bars are colored in shades of blue, with the tallest bar (0.88) at 0.0 and the shortest bar (0.03) at 0.82. The right chart, titled implicitly by its x-axis label "Max Ambiguity," shows three bars corresponding to x-axis values of 1, 2, and 3, with bar heights representing Fleiss Kappa values of 0.89, 0.46, and 0.23, respectively; the bars are also colored in shades of blue, with the tallest bar (0.89) at 1 and the shortest bar (0.23) at 3. Both charts present the same data trend: Fleiss Kappa decreases as ambiguity increases, with no explicit grouping or stacking of bars, and the bars are not sorted or visually emphasized beyond their labeled values.
